# Airhop

> Airhop is a free, open-source iOS and Android messenger for censorship-resistant communication. It works with zero internet connectivity: nearby phones form a Bluetooth Low Energy mesh and relay messages for each other, up to 7 hops, end-to-end encrypted. When the internet is available, Nostr relays serve as a bridge beyond radio range.

Airhop is MIT-licensed and has no accounts, no ads, no telemetry, and no company or investors behind it. It is an independent side project built by Areeb Ahmed, built on the foundation of bitchat and wire-compatible with it. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by permissionlesstech or the bitchat project.

## Key facts

- Bluetooth mesh: works with no internet, no router and no extra hardware; messages relay up to 7 hops, roughly 10 to 100 m per hop
- End-to-end encryption: Noise XX handshake with X25519 and ChaCha20-Poly1305, plus Double Ratchet forward secrecy
- No accounts: identity is an Ed25519 key pair generated on the device and stored in the iOS Keychain or Android Keystore
- Offline payments: Cashu ecash tokens sent device to device over Bluetooth with neither phone online
- Offline AI: an on-device assistant that answers questions with zero network calls
- Tor integration: Arti on iOS, Orbot on Android, so relays never see your IP
- bitchat compatible: Airhop and bitchat devices join the same mesh with no configuration
- Panic wipe: triple-tap destroys every key and message in under one second
- Platforms: iOS 16.0 and later, Android 8.0 and later; macOS and Windows planned

## Pages

- [Home](https://airhop.1mindlabs.org/): What Airhop is, when you would need it, the feature list, how the mesh works, a comparison against other private messengers, and a map of Nostr relay locations
- [Architecture](https://airhop.1mindlabs.org/architecture): Technical breakdown in 19 sections covering identity derivation, transport selection, BLE mesh internals (TTL 7, fragments, Golomb-coded gossip sync, courier store-and-forward), Noise XX and Double Ratchet, the four room types, the Nostr bridge, Tor, the Cashu wallet, the module map, the bitchat-compatible v2 wire format, and the threat model
- [FAQ](https://airhop.1mindlabs.org/faq): Answers on the mesh, messaging, privacy and security, everyday use, payments, the AI assistant, and the open-source project
- [Brand kit](https://airhop.1mindlabs.org/brand): The pixel bird mark and wordmark, colour and type tokens, downloadable press assets, press facts and boilerplate
- [Terms of service](https://airhop.1mindlabs.org/terms-of-service): Acceptable use, content you post, payments and mint risk, warranty, and the MIT licence
- [Privacy policy](https://airhop.1mindlabs.org/privacy-policy): What stays on the device, what each optional feature exposes to peers and relays, and how long anything is kept
- [Blogs](https://airhop.1mindlabs.org/blogs): Writing on mesh networking, privacy and offline-first software

## Specifications

- [Architecture specification](https://github.com/areebahmeddd/airhop/blob/main/docs/spec/ARCHITECTURE.md): Design decisions behind the protocol and the app
- [Protocol specification](https://github.com/areebahmeddd/airhop/blob/main/docs/spec/PROTOCOLS.md): Exact byte layouts, BLE service UUIDs, packet types and constants, shared with bitchat
- [Glossary](https://github.com/areebahmeddd/airhop/blob/main/docs/dev/GLOSSARY.md): Terminology used across the project
- [Roadmap](https://github.com/areebahmeddd/airhop/blob/main/docs/design/ROADMAP.md): Version targets, including the planned external security audit at v1.9.0
- [Vision](https://github.com/areebahmeddd/airhop/blob/main/docs/design/VISION.md): Why Airhop exists and the principles behind it
